html:
Swami Vivekananda was a Hindu monk from Calcutta, born Narendranath Datta in 1863, who brought Vedanta and yoga to Western audiences and helped shape modern Hinduism.

As a young man he was drawn to the Brahmo Samaj and to Western philosophy. Then he met the mystic Ramakrishna, who became his teacher. After Ramakrishna's death in 1886 he took vows as a monk and wandered across India.

In September 1893 he spoke at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago, opening with "Sisters and brothers of America". The speech made him famous, an event shown on the chart as Vivekananda in Chicago. He lectured for years in the United States and Britain, teaching Advaita Vedanta and a form of yoga as a path open to anyone.

Back in India he founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 to join spiritual life with service: schools, hospitals and famine relief. He died in 1902, aged 39. His call for self confidence and service inspired a generation of Indian nationalists, and his birthday is India's National Youth Day.
